native_result.query: Between which years did the largest increases in median wealth occur among black females?
native_result.HypoA: The largest increases in median wealth from 1985 to 1990 were among black females, with a percentage increase of 1385.71%.
native_result.HypoB: Among black females in the NLS 1979 cohort (n=1,548), the largest adjacent-wave increase in median composite wealth occurred between 1985 and 1990, when the median rose from $175 to $2,600 (+$2,425), exceeding the 1990–1996 change of +$1,400; the cumulative 1985–1996 change of +$3,825 is noted only as a secondary diagnostic spanning the two adjacent intervals.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded data/nls_incarceration_processed.csv (12,013 rows, 6 cols, zero missingness across all columns). Filtered to race=='black' AND sex=='female' (n=1,548; per-year valid N=1,548 for all three wealth columns). Kept negative and zero composite wealth values (NLS debt convention). Computed raw medians at each wave: 1985=$175, 1990=$2,600, 1996=$4,000. Computed three pairwise median differences — adjacent: Δ(1990−1985)=+$2,425, Δ(1996−1990)=+$1,400; full-span diagnostic: Δ(1996−1985)=+$3,825. Identified the largest adjacent-wave increase as 1985→1990. Robustness footnote: BF raw means are 1985=$10,646.94, 1990=$24,496.24, 1996=$42,691.89, under which the largest adjacent increase flips to 1990→1996 (mean Δ +$18,195.65 vs +$13,849.30); the median-led hypothesis is unchanged. No bootstrap CI, no winsorisation, no log-transform, no re-derivation of the composite.

sub_hypo.text: Among black females in the NLS 1979 cohort (n=1,548), the largest adjacent-wave increase in median composite wealth occurred between 1985 and 1990: from $175 to $2,600 (+$2,425), exceeding the 1990–1996 increase from $2,600 to $4,000 (+$1,400). The cumulative 1985–1996 increase of $3,825 is a secondary diagnostic spanning both adjacent intervals.
sub_hypo.context: Black female respondents in the NLS 1979 cohort (race=='black' and sex=='female'; n=1,548, with valid wealth observations for all three waves). Raw wealth values include negative and zero values; no winsorisation, log transformation, or composite re-derivation was performed.
sub_hypo.relations: Median composite wealth increased across all three waves, with the 1985–1990 increase (+$2,425) greater than the 1990–1996 increase (+$1,400). The full-span 1985–1996 increase (+$3,825) is secondary and is not ranked against adjacent-wave increases. This ordering is median-specific: the robustness comparison using raw means reverses the ordering, with a larger adjacent increase in 1990–1996 (+$18,195.65) than in 1985–1990 (+$13,849.30).
